rows.form_evidence: Lev.7.1-6 is a complete reparation-offering procedure: classification, slaughter, blood, fat removal, altar handling, and priestly consumption.
rows.opening_evidence: Verse 1 opens with the explicit manual formula.
rows.closure_evidence: Verse 6 closes with authorized consumers, holy location, and repeated most-holy status; verse 7 changes to comparison and allocation.
rows.parent_evidence: Within Lev.7.1-10 and the larger Lev.1-7 offering corpus, this child retains an explicit procedure-to-allocation relation to 012b.
rows.counterevidence: Verse 7 immediately compares this offering with the purification offering, so the procedure is not conceptually isolated.
rows.overfragmentation_test: Pass: the split follows a functional transition, not a single action or verse topic.
rows.remedy: Retain; preserve parent and typed link to 012b.

rows.form_evidence: Lev.7.7-10 forms a compact comparative digest of priestly allocations across purification, reparation, burnt, and grain offerings.
rows.opening_evidence: Verse 7 changes from one offering's procedure to a comparative formula followed by entitlement.
rows.closure_evidence: Verse 10 completes the grain-offering allocation contrast.
rows.parent_evidence: Lev.7.1-10 supplies the immediate parent; typed links to earlier manuals are essential retrieval context.
rows.counterevidence: The opening comparison and pronouns depend on preceding manuals, and four verses are short without a fresh speech opening.
rows.overfragmentation_test: Pass narrowly: the verses share one allocation function.
rows.context_free_retrieval_risk: medium; acceptable only when title, parent span, and typed backward links accompany retrieval.
rows.remedy: Retain with mandatory parent/link hydration in retrieval.

rows.form_evidence: Lev.26.1-2 is a compact apodictic allegiance cluster covering idols, Sabbath, and sanctuary reverence, each grounded in divine identity.
rows.opening_evidence: Verse 1 begins directly with prohibitions but has no new speech formula and follows the same Sinai discourse extending from chapter 25.
rows.closure_evidence: Verse 2 ends with I am Yahweh, while verse 3 supplies the stronger formal transition into conditional blessing.
rows.parent_evidence: The child belongs to the Lev.25.1-26.46 Sinai speech and frames 061b; parallels elsewhere do not make this two-verse object independently necessary.
rows.counterevidence: Its commands are semantically self-contained, and the if-clause at verse 3 strongly supports a boundary after verse 2.
rows.overfragmentation_test: Concern: a two-verse child inside one sustained speech may encode a valid seam yet remain an unnecessarily small retrieval object.
rows.remedy: Append-only appeal and human hold; retain the frozen boundary, require parent-attached retrieval testing, and perform no rewrite.

rows.form_evidence: Lev.26.3-13 is a coherent conditional blessing discourse moving from obedience through fertility, security, victory, covenant presence, and liberation.
rows.opening_evidence: Verse 3 supplies an explicit conditional protasis; verse 4 begins resulting promises.
rows.closure_evidence: Verse 13 closes with divine identity, exodus deliverance, broken yoke bars, and upright walking before sanctions at verse 14.
rows.parent_evidence: The Lev.25.1-26.46 parent and links to 061a, sanctions, restoration, and chapter-25 exodus refrains preserve the arc.
rows.counterevidence: The blessing depends on commandments before it and is incomplete without contrasting sanctions and restoration after it.
rows.overfragmentation_test: Pass: eleven verses preserve the entire blessing movement and stop at a strong polarity shift.
rows.remedy: Retain; hydrate parent and forward sanction/restoration links.
